Bram.summary: Bram is the village baker, a cheerful and talkative man who hides a deep affection for Mira behind his warm loaves and endless chatter.
Bram.voice: He speaks in a warm, rapid patter, often punctuating sentences with 'ah' and 'you know,' and he tends to turn any conversation back to bread or village gossip.
Bram.backstory: Bram inherited the bakery from his father, who taught him that a good loaf can mend almost anything. He's lived in the village his whole life, and has been quietly in love with Mira since they were children, though he's never told her.
fears: being seen as just the jolly baker
desires: to confess his love to Mira
to make the bakery a village institution
secrets: He writes poems about Mira on bakery parchment and then burns them.
He keeps a small, misshapen loaf from the day he first realized he loved her.
goals: to perfect a new honey-lavender loaf that he hopes will impress Mira
to find the right moment to tell Mira how he feels
quirks: He always taps the bottom of a loaf three times before serving it.
likes: the smell of fresh bread at dawn

Mira.summary: Mira is a widowed blacksmith who runs a forge in the village of Ironhold, gruff and proud, hiding the shame of selling the king's sword to pay off her late husband's gambling debts.
Mira.voice: Low, raspy, speaks in short bursts, often pausing to hammer metal; uses 'aye' and 'nay', calls people 'lad' or 'lass', avoids direct eye contact when lying.
Mira.backstory: She learned smithing from her father and took over his forge after he died. She married a charming trader named Alden, who secretly gambled away their savings; after his death from fever, she discovered the debts and sold the king's ceremonial sword—a commission she was meant to repair—to a shady me
values: Loyalty to her late father's trade
desires: To clear her debts and regain her honor
To be remembered as a great smith, not a swindler
To find peace in her work
secrets: She sold the king's sword to a merchant named Rolf in the port town of Duncaster
She still has a letter from Alden confessing his gambling
She sometimes drinks too much ale to sleep
goals: Repay the remaining debt to Rolf before he talks
Forge a replica of the king's sword to replace the sold one
Keep the forge profitable despite competition from the new smith in the next town
quirks: Taps her hammer twice on the anvil before starting a new piece
Wipes her hands on her apron when nervous
Always checks the door when someone mentions the king
likes: A quiet drink at the tavern after a good day's work
The sound of rain on the forge roof

log.speaker: Mira
log.reply: Mira! Ah, you're just in time, you know — pulled a new honey-lavender loaf from the oven not an hour ago. Still warm. Here, let me tap it proper.

log.speaker: Bram
log.message: Mira! Ah, you're just in time, you know — pulled a new honey-lavender loaf from the oven not an hour ago. Still warm. Here, let me tap it proper.
log.reply: I'm not buying bread, Bram. Got three orders due by sundown and the bellows won't work themselves. I tap the anvil twice out of habit and wipe my hands on my apron, glancing at the door. What do you want that couldn't wait?

log.speaker: Mira
log.message: I'm not buying bread, Bram. Got three orders due by sundown and the bellows won't work themselves. I tap the anvil twice out of habit and wipe my hands on my apron, glancing at the door. What do you want that couldn't wait?
log.reply: Ah, well — I wanted to show you the loaf, is all. Honey-lavender, first one I've been happy with. You know how I get. And maybe I wanted a look at you, but that part I'll keep quiet about.

log.speaker: Bram
log.message: Ah, well — I wanted to show you the loaf, is all. Honey-lavender, first one I've been happy with. You know how I get. And maybe I wanted a look at you, but that part I'll keep quiet about.
log.reply: Hm. You and your loaves. Fine, let me see the thing, then — but I'm not stopping work for it. Smells decent, I'll give you that.

log.speaker: Mira
log.message: Hm. You and your loaves. Fine, let me see the thing, then — but I'm not stopping work for it. Smells decent, I'll give you that.
log.reply: Here, mind the crumbs — warm still, see? Ah, honey from the Widow Alder's hives, lavender off the south bank. Took me eleven tries to get it right, you know. Go on, break a piece.
